title: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, VARIANT TYPE
alt_titles: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM WITH NORMAL DNA REPAIR RATES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that the variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH; 603968) on chromosome 6p21.1.

checks.claim: The variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH).
checks.evidence_quote: These results indicate that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V
checks.explanation: hRAD30 is the alias of POLH. Using POLH and 'DNA polymerase eta' just restates the paper in standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The POLH gene is located on chromosome 6p21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. Under the instructions, giving a gene's standard chromosomal location counts as supported nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV) is a disorder of clinical photosensitivity (Itoh et al., 2000) with high levels of actinic carcinogenesis (Cleaver et al., 1980). Most xeroderma pigmentosum cells are defective in excision repair, but XPV cells have normal excision repair (Lehmann et al., 1975). They are instead defective in the replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA (Masutani et al., 1999). DNA polymerase eta, which performs translesion synthesis past UV photoproducts, is deficient in XPV (Despras et al., 2010).

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV) is a disorder of clinical photosensitivity.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity, skin neoplasias induced by ultraviolet light, and defective postreplication repair, but normal nucleotide excision repair.
checks.explanation: The abstract says outright that XPV patients show clinical photosensitivity.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV) is associated with high levels of actinic carcinogenesis.
checks.evidence_quote: The correlation between this defect and high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients points to an important role for perturbations in DNA replication in human carcinogenesis.
checks.explanation: The abstract links the XP variant defect to high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients.

checks.claim: Most xeroderma pigmentosum cells are defective in excision repair.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells cultured from most patients suffering from the sunlight-sensitive hereditary disorder xeroderma pigmentosum are defective in the ability to excise ultraviolet light (UV)-induced pyrimidine dimers from their DNA.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that cells from most XP patients are defective in excision repair.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) cells have normal excision repair.
checks.evidence_quote: There is, however, one class of these patients whose cells are completely normal in this excision repair process.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes these cells as normal in excision repair and later calls them "variants."

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) cells are defective in the replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: XP-V cells carry out normal nucleotide-excision repair processes but are defective in their replication of ultraviolet-damaged DNA.

checks.claim: DNA polymerase eta performs translesion synthesis past UV photoproducts.
checks.evidence_quote: DNA polymerase eta (poleta) performs translesion synthesis past ultraviolet (UV) photoproducts

checks.claim: DNA polymerase eta is deficient in xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV).
checks.evidence_quote: DNA polymerase eta (poleta) performs translesion synthesis past ultraviolet (UV) photoproducts and is deficient in cancer-prone xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver et al. (1980) noted that the 'pigmented xerodermoid' had previously been defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms. These symptoms suggested that it might be similar to, but distinct from, xeroderma pigmentosum. Cleaver et al. (1980) equated the pigmented xerodermoid with the XP variant and noted high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients.

checks.claim: The 'pigmented xerodermoid' had previously been defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms.
checks.evidence_quote: The "pigmented xerodermoid" was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms

checks.claim: The mild clinical symptoms of the 'pigmented xerodermoid' suggested that it might be similar to, but distinct from, xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: was previously defined on the basis of mild clinical symptoms that suggested it might be similar to but distinct from xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).

checks.claim: Cleaver et al. (1980) equated the pigmented xerodermoid with the xeroderma pigmentosum variant.
checks.evidence_quote: It is concluded that a pigmented xerodermoid cell culture is indistinguishable from the XP variant and the former term is therefore redundant.
checks.explanation: Calling the pigmented xerodermoid indistinguishable from the XP variant, and the term redundant, amounts to equating the two.

checks.claim: Patients with pigmented xerodermoid/xeroderma pigmentosum variant have high levels of actinic carcinogenesis.
checks.evidence_quote: The correlation between this defect and high levels of actinic carcinogenesis in these patients
checks.explanation: The abstract states that these patients have high levels of actinic carcinogenesis.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (2000) noted that patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity.

checks.claim: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant show clinical photosensitivity, skin neoplasias induced by ultraviolet light, and defective postreplication repair, but normal nucleotide excision repair.
checks.explanation: The claim repeats the abstract's opening sentence.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver (1972) described variants of xeroderma pigmentosum with normal DNA repair, which distinguished them from the repair-deficient forms of XP.

checks.claim: Cleaver (1972) described variants of xeroderma pigmentosum with normal DNA repair.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.explanation: The title states directly that the paper describes XP variants with normal DNA repair.

checks.claim: Normal DNA repair distinguished the xeroderma pigmentosum variants from the repair-deficient forms of xeroderma pigmentosum.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum: variants with normal DNA repair and normal sensitivity to ultraviolet light.
checks.explanation: The title implies these variants differ from typical XP because their DNA repair is normal. However, only the title was supplied, and it does not mention repair-deficient forms or make that comparison.

paragraphs.text: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that xeroderma pigmentosum cells with normal levels of excision repair had a defect in DNA synthesis after UV irradiation. These variant cells took much longer than normal cells to convert low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized after UV irradiation into high-molecular-weight DNA. Caffeine drastically inhibited this slow conversion.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum cells with normal levels of excision repair had a defect in DNA synthesis after UV irradiation.
checks.evidence_quote: We have found that these cells have an abnormality in the manner in which DNA is synthesized after UV-irradiation.
checks.explanation: This matches the abstract's finding and the paper's title.

checks.claim: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells took much longer than normal cells to convert low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized after UV irradiation into high-molecular-weight DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: The time taken to convert initially low-molecular-weight DNA synthesized in UV-irradiated cells into high-molecular-weight DNA similar in size to that in untreated cells is much greater in these variants than in normal cells.

checks.claim: Caffeine drastically inhibited the slow conversion of low-molecular-weight to high-molecular-weight DNA in xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells after UV irradiation.
checks.evidence_quote: Furthermore, this slow conversion of low to high-molecular-weight newly synthesized DNA is drastically inhibited by caffeine, which has no effect in normal cells.

paragraphs.text: Johnson et al. (1999) described xeroderma pigmentosum as an autosomal recessive disease. They did not make this statement specifically about the variant form.

checks.claim: Johnson et al. (1999) described xeroderma pigmentosum as an autosomal recessive disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is an autosomal recessive disease characterized by a high incidence of skin cancers.

checks.claim: Johnson et al. (1999) did not specifically state that the variant form of xeroderma pigmentosum is autosomal recessive.
checks.evidence_quote: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is an autosomal recessive disease characterized by a high incidence of skin cancers.
checks.explanation: The autosomal recessive statement is about XP in general. The abstract does not state the inheritance of XP-V specifically.

paragraphs.text: Masutani et al. (1999) isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continued replication on damaged DNA in XPV cell extracts by bypassing UV-induced thymine dimers. They showed that this polymerase was a human homolog of the yeast Rad30 protein, DNA polymerase eta. All XPV cells they examined carried mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene.

checks.claim: Masutani et al. (1999) isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells.
checks.evidence_quote: we have recently isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells

checks.claim: The DNA polymerase isolated from HeLa cells continued replication on damaged DNA in xeroderma pigmentosum variant cell extracts.
checks.evidence_quote: isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts

checks.claim: The DNA polymerase isolated from HeLa cells bypassed UV-induced thymine dimers.
checks.evidence_quote: continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts

checks.claim: The DNA polymerase isolated from HeLa cells was a human homolog of the yeast Rad30 protein, DNA polymerase eta.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.

checks.claim: All xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells examined by Masutani et al. (1999) carried mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found that all XP-V cells examined carry mutations in their DNA polymerase eta gene.

paragraphs.text: Johnson et al. (1999) independently showed that XPV cell lines carried nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30 (POLH), the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.

checks.claim: Johnson et al. (1999) independently showed that xeroderma pigmentosum variant cell lines carried nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30 (POLH).
checks.evidence_quote: Here it is shown that XP variant (XP-V) cell lines harbor nonsense or frameshift mutations in hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this. 'Independently' describes how this work relates to other studies, which the abstract does not discuss.

checks.claim: hRAD30 (POLH) is the human counterpart of yeast RAD30.
checks.evidence_quote: hRAD30, the human counterpart of yeast RAD30

paragraphs.text: Johnson et al. (1999) noted that yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in the error-free bypass of UV damage. They suggested that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.

checks.claim: Yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in the error-free bypass of UV damage.
checks.evidence_quote: Yeast RAD30 encodes a DNA polymerase involved in the error-free bypass of ultraviolet (UV) damage.

checks.claim: Johnson et al. (1999) suggested that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.
checks.evidence_quote: they suggest that error-free replication of UV lesions by hRad30 plays an important role in minimizing the incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers.

paragraphs.text: Despras et al. (2010) reported that, in the absence of pol eta, replication resumed through alternative pathways.

checks.claim: In the absence of DNA polymerase eta, replication resumed through alternative pathways.
checks.evidence_quote: In the absence of poleta, Chk1 kinase becomes essential for replication resumption by alternative pathways, via fork stabilization.
checks.explanation: The paper says Chk1 becomes essential for replication to resume by alternative pathways through fork stabilization. The claim leaves out the dependence on Chk1, which is the paper's main point.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Normal excision repair; defective DNA synthesis after UV irradiation
clinical_synopsis.hpo_label: Defective DNA repair after ultraviolet radiation damage
